A fresh `bd init` in an isolated HOME/GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/DOLT_ROOT_PATH fixture creates NO .beads/beads.db, no -wal and no -shm — the store is .beads/embeddeddolt/beads and the doctor's own query returns schema 53 — and `bd doctor` against it moves the whole of .beads/ by 0 added / 0 removed. ARM 2, bd 1.3.0 (the ceiling and this host's own bd): same result, no SQLite trio, `bd doctor` 0/0. POSITIVE CONTROL on every arm, run immediately after each measurement on the identical `find .beads | sort` instrument: a deliberate `touch` showed up as exactly 1 added, so an empty delta was meaningful. CORROBORATION ON REAL DATA, not only fixtures: this repository's own live .beads/ — months of history, an 11MB issues.jsonl — contains issues.jsonl and NO beads.db, beads.db-wal or beads.db-shm. ARCHAEOLOGY with a positive control: `git log --all --reverse -S'beads.db-wal'` returns exactly ONE commit for the doctor and exactly one for the skill — ff38ee8, 2026-07-28 — while the same pipeline over `DOCTOR_BD_SCHEMA` returns several, so a single hit is a result rather than a broken search. So the WAL inventory was taken in the bd-0.47.x era, when SQLite was the primary store (this repo's own .beads/.gitignore says so: 'SQLite databases (bd <= 0.47.x primary store)' vs 'Embedded Dolt store (bd >= 1.1.x primary store)'), and has never been re-taken. THE BOUND IS STATED RATHER THAN ELIDED: this is NOT universally false. The doctor still accepts bd >= 0.47 (DOCTOR_MIN_BD_VERSION="0.47"; install.sh MIN_BD_VERSION="0.47"), and on a target whose store was created by such a bd the SQLite files do exist and the sentence holds. I did not test bd 0.47.x.

findings.evidence: The new scoping sentence reads: 'So the run below could not have exercised the SELECT, and it is evidence about the three .beads/* WAL files ONLY — not a complete inventory of what a full run touches today.' Three lines later the SAME measurement is cited for a SECOND proposition: ':71-72 the same run with `--skip beads` left all 6,936 files byte-identical', and the paragraph closes ':82-83 So `--skip beads` is the run that provably touches nothing — use it on a read-only mount, mid-`bd` operation, or when you need that guarantee.' Both cannot stand: either the run is evidence about the three WAL files ONLY, in which case the `--skip beads` arm is not evidence and the word 'provably' has no support left in this surface, or it is also evidence about the 6,936-file arm and the word ONLY is wrong. The two arms share one provenance — `git log --all --reverse -S'6,936'` returns exactly ONE commit repo-wide, ff38ee8 (verified; the same pipeline returns one commit for '10,358' too, and multiple for control strings) — so the header's own reasoning about staleness applies to the `--skip beads` arm verbatim and is not applied to it. WHAT IS NOT WRONG, and is why this sits at medium rather than higher: the operational claim is TRUE and is independently supported. I verified structurally that `--skip beads` really does skip the SELECT — the `dolt sql` call at :1538-1539 is inside check_beads(), whose body runs :1391-1595, and the dispatcher's `is_skipped` test at :2289 `continue`s before check_beads is ever invoked — and that structural reason IS stated in --help :409-410, in the skill :67-69 and in the new comment :1476-1479. It is missing from exactly one surface: the header, which is the surface that withdraws the measurement.
findings.description: Rubric C9 (.claude/rubrics/default.md v3): 'a claim that OVERSTATES a defect fails like one that understates it', and C9's own rationale is that pessimistic errors survive review because 'it's worse than I said' feels conservative. This is that error. The sentence withdraws more evidential value than the facts require and the file then contradicts it three lines on, leaving an operator who reads to the end of the paragraph with a 'provably' whose stated proof the same paragraph has just voided. NOT A v5.0.0 BLOCKER under the stated stop rule: the claim it undercuts is independently true, structurally proven, and correctly supported in the other three surfaces, so nothing a reader acts on is false. The cheapest honest repair is one clause — scope the ONLY to the beads-check arm, or carry the structural reason into the header the way --help already does. v5.0.1.

findings.evidence: Each corrected surface OPENS its correction with an attribution the same paragraph then contradicts. --help :401: 'A FOURTH effect the original measurement missed'. Skill :56-57: 'A FOURTH effect was missed by the original measurement'. Five lines later, --help :405-408: 'The original 6,936-file run reported three files and nothing else because it PREDATES this SELECT entirely (the figure entered 2026-07-28, the SELECT 2026-08-16) — not because stats happened to pre-exist'; skill :63-65: 'The original 6,936-file measurement saw nothing because it PREDATES this SELECT entirely ... so it never covered this effect.' A measurement cannot MISS an effect produced by code that did not exist when it ran. I re-derived the ordering rather than reading it: `git show ff38ee8:.claude/scripts/workflow-doctor.sh | grep -c -i dolt` returns 0, with THREE positive controls on the identical pipeline and the identical input — `check_beads` 3, `6,936` 3, `10,358` 2, over a 1,522-line file — so the zero is a result and not a broken search; `-S'schema_migrations'` first returns 33e45fa (2026-08-16), whose added line IS `dolt sql -r csv -q "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version),0) FROM schema_migrations"`; `-S'dolt'` first returns fdfd6ce (2026-08-03), whose four added matches are all prose/heredoc references to `bd dolt status`, not an executed dolt call. So no dolt command existed in the file before 33e45fa.
findings.description: 'Missed' is the precise framing FIX A exists to remove, surviving in the first sentence of FIX A's own correction on both surfaces. It tells a reader the 2026-07-28 run was taken against code that contained the SELECT and overlooked one of its effects — which is exactly what keeps that measurement reading as current, and what round 3 recorded as R3-F1. NOT A BLOCKER: both surfaces correct themselves inside the same paragraph, so a reader who finishes it ends up with the right model, and the resulting inventory (four effects) is identical either way. Recorded because it is the residue of the exact defect this round exists to confirm closed, and because one word closes it ('uncovered', or 'an effect the original measurement predates'). v5.0.1.

AND I CHECKED THE SUCCESSOR STORY IS NOT ITSELF UNVERIFIABLE: every premise it rests on (two commit hashes, two dates, one grep result) is checkable, is stated in the text, and checked out. The one claim in the replacement that is unfalsifiable by construction is ':63-64 and has never been re-taken' — what is observable is that the figure's occurrence count never changed in git; a re-take that produced the same number would leave no trace. Not false, and flagged only because the brief asked for inference-voiced-as-observation. FIX B — THE PROPOSITION DOES NOT SURVIVE ANYWHERE, swept four ways with positive controls. (i) Phrasing sweep over the whole repo including Makefile, docs/, README, agent prompts, .github/, the component tier and the e2e tier: 'only file change|ONLY things a full run|only thing a full run|exactly those three|modifies nothing at all|changed nothing at all|provably touches nothing|touches nothing|6,936|10,358' -> 25 hits, every one accounted for. (ii) A second sweep on 'read-only|READ.ONLY|writes nothing|never writes|does not write|modifies no |modifies nothing|no side.effect|side.effect free|byte-identical' filtered to doctor context -> 37 hits, same conclusion. (iii) A third over 'beads.db-wal|beads.db-shm|CHECKPOINT|checkpoint' -> the tighter net any inventory restatement must fall into. WHAT REMAINS, and why none of it is the proposition: Makefile:470-476, docs/QUICKSTART.md:191-196, docs/HOOKS.md:3050 and docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md:822 each describe the beads exception and each states only the narrower claim '`--skip beads` ... provably touches nothing', which is TRUE and which I verified structurally (the SELECT is inside check_beads and the dispatcher skips the function wholesale). None of the four asserts exclusivity over file changes — no 'only', no 'nothing else', no 'exactly those three'. They are INCOMPLETE inventories (none mentions .dolt/stats), which is v5.0.1 sweep material and is named here so the next pass knows where to land; they are not restatements of the withdrawn claim. The two sentences round 3 filed as R3-F2 are both genuinely rewritten: :61-69 now scopes the measurement explicitly, and :1375-1384 now opens 'This is NOT the only file change a full run makes'. FIX C — THE REPLACEMENT MAKES NO COUNT AND NO EXPLICIT COMPLETENESS CLAIM, and the one claim it makes BY IMPLICATION is true on the sweep above. The count is deleted, not corrected, exactly as the brief says. The single implicature is :1471-1472 'Other surfaces stating this check's side-effect inventory carried the same error and were corrected with it' — a bare plural in the past tense, which reads as 'the other surfaces that carried it were corrected'. It is immediately defeated by the two sentences that follow ('A COUNT of them is deliberately NOT given ... a wrong count reads as a completed audit. Grep the proposition, not this comment.'), and on my independent sweep it is TRUE: no surface anywhere in the repo still carries the error. The second, weaker implicature is the cleft at :1476-1477 ('What is genuinely unaffected IS ...'), whose content I verified structurally. So the answer to the brief's question is: one weak completeness claim by implication, defeated in the next sentence and true on measurement.
